c.tagline: Where volcano meets sea in the heart of the Indian Ocean.

taxi.fareNote: Shared taxis (taxis collectifs) run set in-town routes for a fixed per-seat fare; private/whole-car hires are negotiated up front since meters are not used.

emergency.note: Emergency response can be slow and under-resourced; serious medical cases are often referred to private clinics (e.g., Clinique Al-Amal) or evacuated to Réunion/Madagascar. Fire brigade can be reached at +269 772 03 73.

hood_landmark.Coulée: Stade Omnisports Said Mohamed Cheikh, Moroni

hood_desc: The historic walled old town of narrow coral-stone lanes around the Friday Mosque and the port; suits culture-focused travelers who want to be within walking distance of the market, mosques and ferries.
Moroni's loudest, most commercial quarter, built around the city's largest open-air market; a good low-cost base for backpackers who don't mind noise and want to be near shared-taxi stands.
The port and seafront corniche district with fishing boats and a coastal promenade, a short walk from the old town; suits travelers wanting central, mid-range hotels near the harbor.
A quieter beach quarter a few kilometers north of downtown with black volcanic-sand beaches and Moroni's main resort-style hotels; ideal for travelers prioritizing pools, sea views and comfort.
A residential district built on an old lava flow near the national stadium, home to guesthouses and long-stay apartments; suits longer-term visitors wanting a calmer, local feel away from downtown.

water.note: Tap water is unsafe for tourists; drink bottled or filtered water.

transit.pay: Cash only (Comorian francs); shared-taxi and minibus fares are paid in cash directly to the driver or a fare collector, with per-seat prices fixed by route. There is no card or app-based payment system.
transit.hours: No fixed timetables; shared taxis and minibuses run through daylight hours and largely stop before sunset, with little to no service after dark.
transit.note: There is no formal urban transit network; getting around relies on shared taxis, private taxi hire, or walking in the compact city center.

bus: Minibuses to towns and villages (no fixed schedule)
ferry: Maria Galanta ferry to Anjouan and Mayotte (twice weekly)
Cargo/passenger boats to other islands and mainland Africa

airport.name: Prince Said Ibrahim International Airport (HAH)
rentals: No major international chains; a few small local car-hire agencies operate near the airport and in town

transit.m: Shared taxi/minibus into Moroni (~30 min, shared)

tip.r: Tipping is not obligatory or deeply rooted locally, but rounding up bills or leaving a small tip at upscale hotels and restaurants catering to foreigners is appreciated.
